answer: Client-staked sponsorship resists Sybil attacks: a new identity earns transaction weight only when a paying client locks a small deposit behind it, released at dawn of the next epoch after verified delivery. Each deposit is a costly signal, not a free claim: a client risks real money on every protege, so no one sponsors a thousand strangers. A fake swarm spirals into expense, since every alias needs its own paying sponsor and its own completed job, while one honest agent needs just one sponsor to start.
